body: Installed lino-env 0.2.8 declares links-notation ^0.11.2, while the consumer root uses current links-notation 0.25.2. The npm graph keeps a nested 0.11.2 copy and prevents an all-latest own-maintained grammar graph without a potentially unsafe override. Please assess the current parser API, migrate the range with roundtrip and cross-platform configuration tests, and document compatibility. This is a maintenance/deduplication request, not a claim that the old version caused a local app failure. Keep current behavior verified, including existing CRLF regression issue #32. A coordinated lino-arguments dependency migration is requested separately; browser-commander#168 reports its analogous older range. Consumer validation reference: https://github.com/konard/vietnam-accomodation-search/commit/20ac35d50129157769c2460d88ffe564ceab7d73 . No private inputs are involved.
title: Assess and update the Links Notation range for latest consumer interoperability

body:
At the moment we have support of multiple values of the same variable like this:

```
A: value1
A: value2
```

That should be dropped, in favor of rewrite. Meaning after such file is read and interpreted `A` = `value2`.

If we really need to support multiple values (array-like, link references sequence), we can do like this:

```
A: value1 value2
```

or

```
A: (value1 value2)
```

or

```
A: 
  value1
  value2
```

or

or

```
A: (
  value1
  value2
)
```

All valid links notation for `['value1', 'value2']`.

It should be done in both JavaScript and Rust versions, and note that this is breaking change for lino-env packages.

Both code and docs should be updated.
title: We should drop support for multiple values of the same variable name

Based on https://github.com/deep-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/src/lino.lib.mjs

Make a tool, that is able to read and write .lenv files.

Simpliest possible example of the Links Notation ENV file:

```
GITHUB_TOKEN: gh_....
TELEGRAM_TOKEN: 054....
```

So instead of usual `=` we use `: `.

The API should allow to get any env by its reference (name, like GITHUB_TOKEN) (actually last instance of reference/link, because duplicates of references are allowed).

And also to set all instances of reference to a new value.

At the moment we should focus on single links, so the links with only one reference (we will treat it as value).
